paragraphs: Rabbi Yose ben Perida. The beloved disciple of Rabbi Eliezer, as in Eruvin 11b. Hyman quotes the Tosefta there, chapter 1: “An incident in which Rabbi Eliezer went to Rabbi Yose ben Perora, his disciple, at Ublin. He said to him, ‘My son,’” and so on. In the Yerushalmi there, chapter 1, halakha 2, he is called “Yose ben Yose ben Perora.”

notes.text: The heading Perida and the body’s Perora differ; the last citation doubles Yose. Ublin is left unidentified and is not rendered as the Polish city Lublin. These source questions remain open.

The saved whole Venice Eruvin1:2 scalar explicitly names Rabbi Yose ben Yose ben Perorah, Eliezer’s student at Ublin. The whole returned ToseftaEruvin1 scalar instead has bracketed Yosef ben Perida, without his student. These support the doubled Yose and variant names, not one harmonized genealogy or a proven insertion history. Heading Perida, body Perora, and supplied Tosefta quotation remain distinct; Ublin remains unidentified. The earlier Eruvin11b finite name search is not a new whole-folio inspection or proof of universal absence.

Eruvin 11b ends by naming Yose ben Perida, Rabbi Eliezer’s disciple. At the start of 12a, the story continues at Ovelin and includes the address “My son.” The consulted Tosefta Eruvin 1 has “[Yosef] ben Perida” at Ublin and omits “his disciple” in this passage. The Venice Yerushalmi Eruvin 1:2 calls him Yose ben Yose ben Perorah and calls him Eliezer’s disciple. Hyman’s heading Perida and the Perora of his quotation are kept as printed. Ublin remains unidentified.
